changed: PATCH 0.41.5 adds the requested DEV-only two-way homepage-player comparison: A0 and R0 controls plus five cumulative additions and five cumulative removals. Every case is a fresh document with one video, the same immutable same-origin v5 MP4, native controls, inline playback and metadata preloading. It does not replace the homepage player or claim to fix native Safari.

A1–A3 add the retained poster, optional default-off English VTT and actual card CSS to literal native HTML. A4 adds Svelte construction plus connected-node source initialization, explicitly labeled as a combined change. A5/R0 reuse the real homepage MediaCard and Watch button. R1–R5 remove captions, poster, card CSS, custom playback handlers and explicit source initialization in order. R5 versus A0 compares plain Svelte with parser-created video. The test recreation excludes Live authentication/navigation shell, so a baseline that works while the real homepage fails would leave that surrounding context unresolved.

The ordinary homepage now uses generic playback-failure/recovery copy instead of numeric media error, ready and network values. Its playback lifecycle and source are unchanged. Dedicated DEV test pages retain local observational state only. Diagnostic source is moved outside the published asset root; the guarded production build deletes both the older diagnostic page and the new matrix, including stale DEV outputs.

Historical native acceptance at DEV 0.41.4/a72c36fb failed with MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED, HAVE_NOTHING and NETWORK_NO_SOURCE. The same iPhone previously played both literal diagnostic players at 0.41.3 and its separate two-byte fetch returned 206 with the expected two bytes. These observations support a controlled integration comparison, not a proven transport or component root cause. The intended Transcode service is a separate unresolved delivery track; this matrix continues the existing byte-streaming app relay.

At exact app source 3bdd25a8dc2f4b900399594b8d142fbfc6959f13, local checks passed 46 tests across six affected suites, three production-build regression tests, typecheck, 975 legacy UI tests and 118 MJS tests with six existing skips. The native media APIs in component tests are mocked. The final exact-head hosted suite, independent review and actual DEV browser verification are release gates, not results claimed by this source-only record.

Two distinct denominators are tracked. Structural configurations: 12 cases A0–A5 and R0–R5; local automated checks attempted 12, passed 12, failed 0, untested 0, without decoding media. Actual playback scenarios: an iPhone viewer tries native playback on each of those 12 cases, with Watch-button behavior separately noted where present; current candidate deployed-browser and physical-iPhone layers each attempted 0, passed 0, failed 0, untested 12. Structural passes are not playback passes. Human satisfaction, confusion and frustration are NOT MEASURED; sample 0. Production promotion remains held until the actual homepage works on the user’s iPhone and diagnostic surfaces are absent from production output. All 134 older release entries remain byte-preserved.
security: No new media target, authentication/session access, backend route, proxy setting, dependency, migration, binding, DNS, security setting or deployment trigger change. The matrix uses fixed case IDs and fixed approved media assets; no arbitrary URL input, telemetry, credential collection, storage or response-header probes. Observers print only event labels and native numeric state with textContent; each navigation leaves the previous video document. No automatic playback or simultaneous multi-player load is introduced.
